steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The brain has four lobes: Frontal (planning, decision-making, personality, motor control), Parietal (sensory processing, spatial awareness), Temporal (hearing, language comprehension, memory), Occipital (visual processing). Each lobe has specialised functions (localisation of function).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The cerebral cortex is the outer layer of the brain responsible for higher-order functions: thinking, language, memory, perception and consciousness. It is divided into two hemispheres connected by the corpus callosum.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Language areas: Broca's area (left frontal lobe) - speech production. Damage causes Broca's aphasia (slow, non-fluent speech but comprehension is intact). Wernicke's area (left temporal lobe) - language comprehension. Damage causes Wernicke's aphasia (fluent but meaningless speech).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The limbic system: amygdala (emotion, especially fear and aggression), hippocampus (forming new memories - damage causes anterograde amnesia as in case of HM), hypothalamus (regulates hormones, temperature, hunger, and the fight-or-flight response).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the functions of the four lobes of the cerebral cortex. | Explain the difference between Broca's aphasia and Wernicke's aphasia, and what this tells us about localisation of function. | Evaluate whether the brain is best understood through localisation or holism.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: 4 lobes: Frontal (thinking), Parietal (sensing), Temporal (hearing), Occipital (seeing). Broca = speech PRODUCTION (can't speak fluently but understands). Wernicke = speech COMPREHENSION (speaks fluently but makes no sense). Localisation = specific areas for specific functions. Holism = brain works as a whole. Both are partly right.
